purpose: Source-traced, dimensionless functional benchmarks for periodontal attachment restoration; not clinical treatment recommendations.

sources.species_and_model: Rat maxillary first-molar replantation; local PDGF-BB pretreatment; day-21 comparison with non-replanted controls.
sources.sample_basis: Mean mechanical outcomes from groups of 6–10 rats as stated in Figure 2 caption; fracture counts reported by group and time in Table 1.

reported_day21_mechanics.source_wording: mean failure load recovered to 54% of control
mean extensibility recovered to 68% of control
mean stiffness recovered almost to the level of NC
mean toughness recovered to 44% of NC
paper says 2.45 N/mm^2 in PDGF-BB was approximately 76% of 3.39 N/mm^2 control
2.45 divided by 3.39; does not equal the paper's stated approximately 76%

sources.important_limit: The extraction test is not normal chewing; endpoint ratios are group means, not specimen-level data. Ankylosis imaging used a separate n=4 group. Replantation also left abnormal bone-like structures in the pulp in most treated replanted teeth.

sources.species_and_model: Mouse periodontal-ligament progenitors seeded onto denuded rat molar roots and replanted into rat sockets; 8- and 16-week outcomes.
sources.source_access: Primary article abstract/full-text page reviewed; Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returned HTTP 500 during local retrieval, so this study is not represented as a locally downloaded specimen-level dataset.
sources.reported_attachment: All 22 progenitor-treated replanted molars were firmly attached at 8 and 16 weeks; at 16 weeks the paper reports a physiologic periodontal apparatus and displacement similar to wild-type controls.
sources.important_limit: This is an invasive replantation study in rats using mouse progenitor cells; it does not establish a method for repositioning an in-situ, trauma-displaced human tooth or avoiding all short-term stabilization.

reduced_model.name: parallel-load-path identifiability demonstration
reduced_model.units: dimensionless fractions of a hypothetical control tangent stiffness
reduced_model.status: illustrative algebra only; not fitted to these studies and not a finite-element or tissue constitutive model
reduced_model.purpose: Show why recovered apparent stiffness alone cannot distinguish a functional shock-absorbing ligament from a stiff ankylotic bridge. Independent mobility, toughness, attachment histology and bridge measurements are needed.
